主要内容: Puerto Rico invoked Title III of the Promesa Act to initiate a municipal bond market bankruptcy, aiming to restructure $70B debt. Governor Ricardo Rossello cited stalled negotiations with creditors as the reason, stating the restructuring would be the largest in U.S. history. The move freezes lawsuits and facilitates debt restructuring, with the goal of protecting essential services and enabling orderly creditor rights determination. Governor Fortuño plans to continue annual debt payments of $800M, an 80% cut from prior levels. Over the next decade, $3.0B–$3.8B in debt service is due on 11 issues, with general obligation bondholders expecting $10B. Moody's analyst Ted Hampton views the decision as positive for bondholders, though acknowledges potential losses and a lengthy court process. The Ad Hoc Group accused the oversight board of sabotaging talks, comparing the situation to Argentina. The restructuring will halt Puerto Rico's economy for years, with the governor losing control over the process.
